items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: We had Gideon Honore on Piano

ctx.x: So you know, well after that, when the job folded we fooled around for a while, and then I got a call from a guy by the name of Floyd Campbell. Floyd Campbell was a pretty popular band leader around Chicago at that time, and he wanted me to work in a place called The Panama, on 58th Street. They used to call 58th Street Dodge City, it was so

bad, you know.
Anyway, I went down to work with Floyd at the Panama, and we had a pretty good little combination. We had Gideon Honore on Piano, and Floyd Campbell on drums, and Jabo Smith on trumpet, and of course myself. And Jabo Smith never made time. He would always come in late, and when he would come in late he'd have to go get something to eat, so he would go downstairs and eat.

Then after he ate he would have to take a little nap. Well by that time, after he woke up, then he would come up and start playing. Well it was almost time for the other bands to get off from their jobs, and they used to come by and hear this combo, and especially to hear Jabo Smith play. And he would wake up, and this cat would blow so much trumpet, he had so much talent it wasn't even funny.
